original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: For every even rotation period n, exact formal F2[D_{2n}] diagonal targets r^k_i x^e_i with only paid reflections x,y, arbitrary binary rank-one idempotents, free scalar mixing, and arbitrary finite restored dirty workspace: determine the sharp separate letter tariffs by balanced address-cut rank.
scope_change_reason: Instantiate the emitted nonabelian-family variation with even finite dihedral groups, changing the abelian rational address premise and closing PR1911's explicit torsion-aware lower-bound question. Unlike another finite register census, the proposed theorem covers all word lengths, even periods, heterogeneous targets and dirty-workspace counts.
bottleneck_link: A formal-model side result screening a nonabelian sharing route before physical synthesis. Even granting free scalar mixing and arbitrary dirty workspace, a sharp direct-word floor rules out local compression in this alphabet. No selected supplier or kappa improvement follows.
stop_rule: Prove the two valid finite-group representations, exact per-call cut ranks, crossing-rank subadditivity, and simultaneous formal attainability before accepting the theorem. Corroborate n=2,6,10 parity boundaries and every target for even n through 32; stop this fixed question after complete proof and bounded controls, without expanding a failed search.
evidence: Written torsion-aware cut-rank theorem with simultaneous full-formal attaining words. Exact research run: 47,872 representation products, 1,088 target cut ranks, 155 rank-one projectors, 1,027 forward/inverse dirty fixtures, 134,864 faithful regular basis columns, 9,420 complete short mixed words, 9,249 omission controls and 13 additional scope/semantic controls. Reproduce via VERIFY.json; final exercised commands and environment are in VALIDATION.json.
author: Adam Gall, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: OpenAI Codex GPT-6 Astra assisted research, proof, implementation and writing; no independent human or proof-assistant verification is implied.
optimistic_full_budget: For target r^k x^e, d_n(k+e) x calls and d_n(k) y calls, summed over all target roles; scalar mixing granted free, all workspace dirty and fully restored. Attaining coordinate word needs no workspace, COPY, free address relabeling, or uncharged restoration. Physical compiler/hosting/tape costs remain unestablished, not zero.
falsification: Any invalid presentation relation, non-coordinate projector whose active cut rank exceeds one, target crossing-rank mismatch, subadditivity failure, or wrong formal boundary falsifies the claimed derivation.
